content.overview: A proposal (offer) when accepted becomes a promise. Communication, revocation, and acceptance rules under sections 3–9 determine when parties are bound.

sections.heading: Offer and invitation to treat
sections.body: An offer is capable of acceptance so as to form a promise. Catalogues, advertisements, and price lists are often invitations to treat, not offers.

sections.heading: Communication and revocation
sections.body: Communication of proposal, acceptance, and revocation follows sections 3–5. A proposal may be revoked before acceptance is complete as against the proposer. Acceptance must be absolute and unqualified (s. 7).

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the communication chain: when the offer was made, how accepted, and whether revocation arrived in time. Electronic contracts need proof of dispatch and receipt under IT and BSA rules.

illustrations: A posts a proposal to sell goods and B posts an unconditional acceptance; the legal effect is determined by sections 3–7 on communication, completion, revocation and absolute acceptance.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 2–9 define proposal, acceptance, promise, consideration and related terms and regulate communication, completion, revocation, absolute acceptance, acceptance by performance and express or implied promises.

Definition: Offer and acceptance form the statutory foundation of agreement formation: a proposal becomes a promise when accepted, subject to the communication and revocation rules.

Ingredients:
1. Identify a definite proposal.
2. Establish acceptance by the offeree in the manner permitted by law.
3. Apply communication and completion rules.
4. Test revocation before completion.
5. Ensure acceptance is absolute and unqualified.
6. Apply performance-based acceptance where section 8 governs.
